learning_outcomes.text: Possess broad and integrated knowledge and understanding of the scope and main areas of Software Engineering and have participated in teams in the realization of software projects.
Have comprehensive knowledge of independent planning, execution, and implementation of a software project and the procedures for professional information exchange.
Have relevant knowledge of the procedures, methods, and tools for carrying out complete software projects. They can systematically use typical tools from software development processes.

Apply a range of software techniques to solve the given software development tasks: procedural models, analysis, definition, implementation, and the use of software tools are mastered. They are able to take on their role in the software development process within the respective procedural models of companies.

Analyze the task, design development questions and hypotheses for approaching a possible solution. They research existing development approaches and solutions. They critically evaluate these and develop new approaches and solutions optimized for the specific task. They highlight the innovative components of their solutions. They create concrete, novel solutions for the task.

Identify complex job-related tasks and communicate professionally with experienced colleagues and clients. They are able to adapt to clients from other departments and competently support them in solving the given task using Software Engineering methods. Through the experience of teamwork in the project and accompanying project supervision, they possess the social competence to address communicative problems in project work. They can present their development results and artifacts, especially at project milestones.

Bring technical-scientific approaches from their experiences into their project work. They can evaluate subject- and task-specific methods with regard to technical and economic aspects. Through collaboration with internal and external university personnel and institutions, they professionalize their communication. They develop their software-technical approach to new tasks, even if these are in new subject areas for them.

syllabus_topics: Processes, procedural models and project roles
Project planning, tracking and project organization
assessment_rules: The theoretical parts of the course, taught during the lecture phase, are assessed throughout the semester through work samples. The creation of programs and documentation of the project in a team also includes the presentation of milestones and the overall project at a project fair after completing the programming task. The supervisor acts as the client/customer. The artifacts created in the individual phases of the software development project are evaluated from both a technical and software engineering perspective. The graded examination is a written project report of approx. 10-20 pages. The ungraded examination is a written work sample of approx. 6 milestone documents, each 3-5 pages.
